title: What child protection and safeguarding training does KHDA require in Dubai private schools?
description: KHDA rules for Dubai private schools: child protection and safeguarding induction before teaching, staff vetting, the code of conduct and mandatory reporting.
shortAnswer: The Knowledge and Human Development Authority (KHDA) requires Dubai private schools to have a KHDA approved student safety and protection policy (Executive Council Resolution No. (2) of 2017, Article 24) and, under its guide for appointing teaching staff, requires every new teacher to complete Child Protection and Safeguarding induction training before teaching. Every staff member must sign the KHDA approved Code of Conduct, and educators are mandatory reporters under Federal Law No. 3 of 2016.
keyTakeaways: Article 24 of Executive Council Resolution No. (2) of 2017 requires a clear, transparent student safety and protection policy approved by KHDA, and makes the school responsible for students on site, on buses and on off site activities.

KHDA's teacher appointment FAQs list Child Protection and Safeguarding among five induction topics new teachers must complete before they begin teaching, with no exemption for similar courses taken elsewhere.

Administrative Resolution No. (54) of 2025 requires KHDA approval before any school staff member starts work, a certificate of good conduct, and a written undertaking to follow the professional and ethical code of conduct.
Schools must notify KHDA within 24 hours of a teacher's warning, dismissal or resignation, and staff dismissed for safeguarding breaches can be placed on KHDA's Deregistration List.
Article 42 of Federal Law No. 3 of 2016 on child rights (Wadeema's Law) makes notification mandatory for educators who see a threat to a child's physical, psychological, moral or mental integrity.
jurisdiction: United Arab Emirates: Emirate of Dubai
regulator: Knowledge and Human Development Authority (KHDA), Government of Dubai
appliesTo: Private schools in the Emirate of Dubai regulated under Executive Council Resolution No. (2) of 2017
Teachers, principals and other school staff who need a KHDA appointment approval
Support staff, who must sign the KHDA approved Code of Conduct
School owners, operators and principals responsible for induction, vetting and reporting

sections.heading: Which Dubai rules require child protection policies and training in private schools?

blocks.text: As at November 2026, three layers apply: a Dubai resolution requiring a protection policy, KHDA appointment rules and guidance requiring induction training, and a federal law making educators mandatory reporters. The anchor is [Executive Council Resolution No. (2) of 2017 Regulating Private Schools in the Emirate of Dubai](https://web.khda.gov.ae/getattachment/About-Us/Legislation/Private-Schools-Regulations/Executive-Council-Resolution-No-(2)-of-2017-Regula/ExecutiveCouncilResolutionNo-(2)of2017RegulatingPrivateSchoolsIntheEmirateOfDubai.pdf.aspx?lang=en-GB). Article 24 states that "A Private School must have a clear and transparent Student safety and protection policy, and implement it upon approval by the KHDA", and that the school is responsible for student safety throughout the school day, on its premises and buses, and during off site activities it organizes.

Article 13 adds general duties that underpin training. A private school must "continuously develop the skills of School Staff" (13.5), appoint qualified staff who meet KHDA requirements (13.15), implement the KHDA approved code of ethics and professional conduct (13.29), and "safeguard and preserve Student rights, and take all necessary action to protect the same" (13.36).

Child protection is also built into licensing. [Administrative Resolution No. (41) of 2026](https://web.khda.gov.ae/getattachment/ee36ff23-c52e-4d86-9b3b-216b57cdd754/Administrative_Resolution_No_41_of_2026_Concerning_the_Requirements_Rules_and_Procedures_for_Issuing_Educational_Permits_for_Private_Schools_En.pdf.aspx?lang=en-GB) on educational permits requires a new school's academic plan to list its policies, including a child protection policy and a recruitment and professional development policy, and to describe its behavioral bylaws, child protection measures and safeguards.

sections.heading: What child protection training must new teachers complete before they teach?

blocks.text: New teachers must complete Child Protection and Safeguarding induction training before they begin teaching. KHDA's [FAQs on the Technical Guide for Appointing Teaching Staff](https://web.khda.gov.ae/getattachment/Guides/Educators/School_Teacher_Recruitment_and_Mobility_FAQs_EN.pdf.aspx?lang=en-GB) list five mandatory induction areas:

items: Understanding UAE culture and laws (for teachers new to Dubai)
Basic security, health, safety, and well-being
Working with Students of Determination (inclusive education)

blocks.text: The school is responsible for organizing these sessions. If it uses external providers, it must choose from KHDA's list of approved providers, and the FAQs state that "This training is subject to audit and evaluation during KHDA visits and inspections."

Previous training does not exempt a new hire. The FAQs say all new staff must complete these trainings "or take an equivalent in-house induction validated by the principal", to keep standards consistent across Dubai private schools. A teacher moving from another Dubai school therefore repeats the induction at the new school, and the principal's validation is the evidence that an in-house equivalent meets the standard.

blocks.title: Status of the FAQs
blocks.text: The induction list appears in KHDA's FAQs on its teacher appointment guide. Administrative Resolution No. (54) of 2025 formally approves the Guide for Appointing Teaching Staff in Private Schools in the Emirate of Dubai, published on KHDA's website. Schools should treat the FAQs as KHDA's explanation of that guide and check the guide itself for any change.

sections.heading: What vetting and code of conduct steps sit alongside the training?

blocks.text: No staff member can start work without KHDA approval, and that approval depends on good conduct evidence and a signed ethics undertaking. [Administrative Resolution No. (54) of 2025](https://web.khda.gov.ae/getattachment/f3b4c9d7-7ad5-4773-8533-afe76e46549f/Admin-Resolution-No-54-of-2025-Concerning-the-Requirements-and-Procedures-for-the-Appointment-of-School-Staff.pdf.aspx?lang=en-GB) sets these conditions in Article 4:

items: good character and repute, evidenced by a valid Dubai Police certificate of good conduct, or, for a non UAE national who has lived in the UAE for less than five years, attested certificates from each country of residence in the previous ten years
a written undertaking to comply with the professional and ethical code of conduct for education professionals issued by the UAE's competent educational authorities
the academic qualifications, experience and expertise set out in the guide

blocks.text: Article 6 requires KHDA's prior approval before the staff member assumes duties, and Article 7 allows KHDA to revoke approval for a breach of the code of conduct. KHDA's FAQs add that every staff member, "including teachers, principals, and support staff", must read and sign the KHDA approved Code of Conduct, which covers professional behavior, child protection and safe use of social media. They also list minimum pre appointment checks, including two written references, police clearance, and confirmation that the candidate is not on KHDA's Deregistration List.

Schools must notify KHDA within 24 hours when a teacher receives a verbal or written warning, is dismissed or resigns. A teacher dismissed for safeguarding breaches, or who resigns to avoid such a dismissal, must be reported for possible deregistration, which generally bars the person from working in any Dubai private school.

sections.heading: Are Dubai school staff legally required to report suspected abuse?

blocks.text: Yes. [Federal Law No. 3 of 2016 on child rights](https://web.khda.gov.ae/getattachment/About-Us/Legislation/Law-No-(2)-of-2021-Concerning-the-Knowledge-and-Hu/Federal-Law-No-3-of-2016-on-child-rights-(Wadeema/Children_Law_English.pdf.aspx?lang=en-GB), known as Wadeema's Law and published on KHDA's legislation page, requires every person to notify a child protection specialist or child protection unit of anything threatening a child's physical, psychological, moral or mental integrity or health (Article 42(1)). Article 42(2) states: "The notification shall be mandatory for the educators, physicians, social specialists or others entrusted with the protection, care or education of the child."

Article 39 provides for child protection units and Article 40 for licensed child protection specialists who take an oath before acting. Training for school staff should therefore cover what counts as a reportable threat, how to report internally and externally, and why the identity of the reporter is protected. The law applies across the UAE, so the reporting content is the same in Dubai and Abu Dhabi even though the school regulators differ.

blocks.text: Neither the resolution nor the FAQs set a fixed refresher interval for child protection training after induction. Schools should set one in policy and justify it; see [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles) and [how to structure onboarding for regulated roles](/guides/how-to-structure-onboarding-for-regulated-roles).

sections.heading: How does KHDA's approach compare with Abu Dhabi and other systems?

blocks.text: KHDA's requirements are built into appointment approval: training before teaching, vetting before duties, and deregistration after breaches. Abu Dhabi's regulator, the Department of Education and Knowledge (ADEK), sets out more detailed policy level requirements, including named child protection roles, a 24 hour reporting rule to its Child Protection Unit, and topic lists for safeguarding induction. See [ADEK teacher licensing and safeguarding](/regulations/adek-abu-dhabi-teacher-licensing-and-safeguarding).

For comparison with other markets, see [US school employee mandated reporter training](/regulations/us-school-employee-mandated-reporter-training) and [working with children check requirements](/regulations/working-with-children-check-requirements). Education providers can find related material on the [higher education and education industry page](/industries/higher-education).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry links each KHDA requirement, from Article 24 to the induction list and Article 42 of Wadeema's Law, to the staff roles it covers and the evidence it needs, before induction content is written. When KHDA updates its appointment guide, the affected induction modules can be identified from those links.

faqs.q: Do teachers moving between Dubai schools need to redo child protection training?
faqs.a: Yes. KHDA's FAQs say all new staff must complete the induction trainings, including Child Protection and Safeguarding, or an equivalent in-house induction validated by the principal, even if they recently completed similar courses elsewhere. The aim is consistent standards across Dubai private schools.

faqs.q: Does the child protection training requirement apply to support staff?
faqs.a: The pre teaching induction list in KHDA's FAQs is framed for new teachers. Separately, every staff member, including support staff, must read and sign the KHDA approved Code of Conduct, which covers child protection. Federal Law No. 3 of 2016 also makes notification mandatory for anyone entrusted with the care or education of a child.

faqs.q: Can a school use any training company for safeguarding induction?
faqs.a: If the school uses an external provider, KHDA's FAQs say it must refer to the list of KHDA approved providers published on the KHDA website. Training delivered in house is acceptable when the principal validates it as equivalent.

faqs.q: What fine applies for failing to protect student rights?
faqs.a: Schedule (2) of Executive Council Resolution No. (2) of 2017 lists a fine of AED 20,000 for failure to protect and preserve the basic rights of students. KHDA can also apply administrative measures under the resolution, and can revoke a staff member's appointment approval for code of conduct breaches.
